text:
maria: Heads up — after the canary deploy today I'm seeing tail OOMs on 2 p100 nodes. Started ~12:03UTC after the inference-service push. :eyes:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Deployed inference-service v1.9.2 to canary (hash=9f3b2a)

aj: Any flamegraphs or heap dumps yet? link please.

maria: Quick profile uploaded to /perf/canary/3751234567/raw.svg — KV working set per-request jumped ~30% on average. Not all requests, looks correlated with long-history chat sessions (large KV lengths).

devon: I dug in — the kernel routing change in v1.9.2 favors `fast-attn-v2` for some sequence shapes. `fast-attn-v2` does a slightly different KV packing (alignment -> extra padding) which increases per-entry allocation. When the batcher keeps forming token-budget 200-300 windows, the aggregate KV footprint jumps and we hit soft oom.

lena: So two levers: (A) limit batch token_budget under high-KV-pressure, (B) fallback kernel selection to the older path when headroom is low. I'm leaning to a combined policy: soft-admit + kernel-fallback.

travis: SGTM. We should prefer admission rather than always falling back to v1 because latency/throughput tradeoffs matter for PLG customers.

maria: Proposed quick config (will iterate in PR):
```json
{
  "batcher": {
    "kv_headroom_threshold_bytes": 536870912, // 512MB
    "max_token_budget_under_kv_pressure": 64,
    "kernel_fallback": {
      "enabled": true,
      "prefer_kernel_when_low_headroom": "fast-attn-v1"
    },
    "soft_evict_non_pinned": true
  }
}
```

aj: How do we cheaply compute `kv_headroom`? Asking because we can't query full allocator stats per-request.

devon: We can use per-GPU watermark metrics from the allocator + recent eviction throughput as a sliding estimate. It's coarse but good enough for admission. Implementation note: sample every 100ms and keep an EWMA; admission uses the latest EWMA.

lena: Also add a safety multiplier for multi-tenant hosts — e.g., kv_headroom_threshold_bytes = min(512MB, 0.25 * total_gpu_kv_limit).

maria: Perf note: switching admitted requests to `fast-attn-v1` under pressure increases median latency ~5% locally but avoids OOMs which cause retries and huge P99 spikes. I think it's an acceptable trade for now.

travis: Can we add a canary plan?
lena: I'll add a rollout: 10% traffic -> monitor OOM count, eviction rate, p99 latency. If OOMs > 0.5% or p99 increases > 20% rollback. Also add a specific regression alert tag `kv-pressure-regress`.

maria: I'll implement the soft-admit logic and kernel-fallback knobs and pair with devon for tests. I'll include a unit test that simulates heavy KV-length traces and verifies cap kicks in.

aj: Please also add an integration prober that runs long-history chats under load to verify no regression in canary.

maria: will do. Opening the PR now and linking the ticket.

incident-bot: incident-bot: Created ticket RN-784 "canary: kv headroom OOMs after v1.9.2" and assigned to maria + devon.

travis: Thanks — keeping this scoped tight. Once PR lands, let's monitor the canary for 2 hours before promoting.

maria: ack. Thanks everyone.
